Definitely check it out. Brighter Shores and its interface handles incredibly well at any window size with a style and music that are very dialed in. If you like incremental games, ironman in Runescape, or a "point-and-click style RPG" (notice the lack of MMO in that statement), I think it's superb. 

The decision-making in the game as to how you're going about the grinds feels significant, but open to preference and there are catch up mechanics in the form of "knowledge" rewards and offline passive training. Being reductionist, everything's "the same", but there are intentional vibe changes across the professions based on the room designs, interaction timings, and how they scale into further progression. If you look for the quirks, you can get a little creative with how you're picking and choosing the nodes and seek out better rates, which involves more observation and strategy. Tricks

I personally really enjoy this game. You can tell it is technically very well made, as it runs well on basically any PC. It also looks great, in my opinion, due to the nice art style.

I realise that the game misses some more dynamic content, but I personally always enjoyed the basic skill grinding in Runescape/OSRS, and the grinding in this game appeals to me as well. Usually I listen to music or do other stuff on my PC while playing, while slowly making progress.

Give it a go if you think you might be interested! I hope the game survives despite the current negative opinions.
Finally a straightforward MMORPG like the original Runescape

As a Runescape addict for 20 years, I'm not sure how I avoided knowing about this game but my friend sent it to me a couple of days ago. I read the negative reviews first and thought "oh well, seems like that doesn't affect me" and decided to play.

A handful of negative reviews I saw said that nobody talks in this game and it's boring. It is repetitive and different from Runescape but I do really like it. You have to go into the game knowing you're NOT playing Runescape and give it a couple of tries. I did at first feel like just getting back on Runescape but after a little bit longer I got hooked here too.

Game good. Good game. Chop wood, turn it into sticks, gather bones ores and stones; turn it all into weapons. Sell everything: Profit. Then buy better tools to make the entire process slightly faster. Rinse and repeat. You're now rich!

You can fight things too, but that's for the peasant rabble. You're not a peasant, are you?
Finally a straightforward MMORPG like the original Runescape

Brighter Shores te mete de recluta novato en la guardia de Hopeport, colega, y de ahí pasas a probar mil oficios como quien cambia de camisa: pesca, minería, herrería, lo que se te ocurra. Se nota que detrás está el creador de RuneScape, porque hay contenido gratis para parar un tren. El problema es que las actualizaciones llegan más despacio que un caracol subiendo una cuesta, y la historia principal es tan recta que apenas te deja decidir nada por tu cuenta. Lleva en acceso anticipado más de un año y todavía le faltan cosas prometidas, así que ve con paciencia. Aun así, para desconectar sin prisa y con oficios para dar y tomar, aquí hay tela para rato.

Very disappointing game. After almost 2 years, there have been only minor quality of life updates and limited content updates. The skilling progression shows similarities to RuneScape, but it is overly sanitized in a way that makes it less engaging and purposeful. For example, Fisherman and Chef are technically related professions, but cooking the fish serves no purpose other than selling them to an NPC. The combat is extremely bland and RNG based, with special attacks still absent to this day. 

One of the worst things about this game is the promotion of the "Lone Wolf" (i.e. Ironman) game mode as a default, or even having it in the game at all. A large percentage of players will never be able to trade or interact with other players in a meaningful way, so what is the point of calling this an MMO? So, I've been following videos and updates on this game for a while, as well as observing the playerbase. Decided to give it a try anyway, being a RS veteran like the rest of you (mostly) I'd imagine. I created a character, some good customization options right off the bat, designed a character I liked, went to name my character aaaannndd.... Paywall! As a F2p player, I was forced to have "#1" after my selected name (ex. HeroName#1) If I was p2p I wouldn't have to have the pesky pound sign and number after my lovely name. Played anyway. I enjoyed a bit of the dialogue in the tut quest, some cheeky lines and personality, and played till I could explore a bit. The exploration is very linear at first, I would imagine it opens more after the into quests, but this is what led me to putting the game down. I actually dropped this game back in 2024 for exactly the reason I'm writing this review now. When I heard about all the new content — new map areas to explore, new professions to try — I got my hopes up and came back expecting things to have changed. A few hours it was interesting, but then it just got boring again. The base problem is not fixed.

👤 The Core Issue Never Left:
More zones, more professions, more surface area... but the same fundamental problem underneath it all. Progress in this game is gated so hard behind profession levels that you can't move forward on quests without grinding first — and that grinding is just repetitive fishing, foraging, cooking, and potion-making with nothing woven in between to make it interesting. Having maxed the game and going through the hardest grinds the game used to have in the past, I can see the direction is getting better. Because it's Andrew Gower myself including most others were more in love with the potential of the game than the game itself which is a big difference. Same as expectation vs reality. It will take time for Andrew Gower to meet us because he's been out of touch with running a successful MMORPG for over a decade and a half and he's not a young stallion he used to be.

I see when Fen releases content, they actually do take feedback but take 2 years to make changes that could have been done a few weeks later worst case scenario. I see this game being a better game by 2030 and if I'm wrong, so be it.

I expect Fen to fix World Events being daily, bi-dai

This is essentially "Watching Paint Dry Simulator". They should have just made a Runescape competitor, cuz this is absurdly boring. Nothing I do feels like it carries any weight. It's all just senseless grinding with no reward goals. The only thing you have to look forward to is unlocking the next training method, which is the same as the last training method, and the training method before that. I wouldn't believe that this game took over a decade to make, had I not spent that decade keeping up with Andrew's Twitter posts about the game/engine. Monumental letdown from the G.O.A.T of the MMO industry, and even more baffling that he's doubling down on the game instead of reworking what people seem to greatly dislike.

This is a baby game, for babies.
There is no adventure here, because it's way too safe. I feel like I'm on rails, and I don't control my own destiny. My character can't just pursue a path I choose, because you are basically forced to play in certain ways.

You can't fight enemies that are too hard for you???
And why do the enemies I was handily beating suddenly start beating me when I level up? So stupid, it completely invalidates my sense of progress.
There is no player economy.

This game had a lot of potential, but I fear it may be too late.
Losing progression every zone is infuriating.

I want to recommend this game to people: I think graphically it's very nice and the skill activities are enjoyable. The combat however is atrocious: the damage calculations work in such a way that even fighting enemies multiple levels lower than you can still result in you losing. Gear also doesn't feel intuitive. Level of gear only matters on gear of the same rarity, anything of a higher rarity will often times be much better than an item of lower rarity that is significantly higher level. This leads to a loop of fighting lower level enemies to kill them quickly so you can get more rolls for higher rarity items instead of being rewarded for moving up the combat ladder. With combat being such an integral part of progression it makes the game feel more like a teeth grinding chore than an enjoyable experience. Hopefully the promised combat updates can bring it to a point where it feels goo
